messages.subject: User-defined Functions within code in NIMBLE

Hi all!

I have two questions that I may need help with.

1. I am fitting a model with NIMBLE, and I have a user defined function in the code defintion. The model has a p dimensional variable and it seems for each iteration it calls the user function p times, whereas I expect it to call it once. I have attached a toy example in this mail. I was hoping I could get help with that.

2. Do we have importance sampler in NIMBLE, or possibly a code that helps in writing one?

Any help will be appreciated.

Regards,
Kwaku

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: User-defined Functions within code in NIMBLE
parts:
hi Kwaku,

1) beta_est depends on each of the beta[j]'s, so since there are P samplers for the beta[j]'s in each iteration, nimblebeta will get called P times.
1a) Side note: If you just need some summary statistic that doesn't place a role directly in the model, it's often best to calculate that post hoc outside of the MCMC.

2) We don't have a basic importance sampler, but we do have a bunch of sequential Monte Carlo algorithms in the nimbleSMC package, some of which involve importance sampling-type calculations. You could look at the code at github.com/nimble-dev/nimbleSMC, but it's plausible it's complicated enough compared to what you are trying to do that it may be more of a distraction than anything else.

-chris
